data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental for Easter 2028? April on the Costa del Sol offers mild temperatures, long sunny days, and a lively atmosphere in Puerto Banús. Whether you're celebrating Semana Santa with family or enjoying a long weekend with friends, knowing the weather patterns helps you choose the right boat and pack smart. This guide breaks down the April climate, sea conditions, and our best charter options so you can lock in your trip with confidence.

Marbella Weather in April 2028: What to Expect

April is a transitional month. Average daily highs reach 21°C, with overnight lows around 12°C. You’ll enjoy roughly 9 hours of sunshine per day, with the sun rising around 07:45 and setting after 20:30 (Spanish summer time). Rainfall is modest — typically 3–4 days of the month, usually as short showers. Winds are generally light westerly at 10–15 knots, calmer in the mornings and picking up slightly in the afternoon. The sea temperature hovers between 16°C and 17°C, so swimming is possible with a wetsuit.

Easter Weekend 2028: Key Dates & Booking Tips

Easter Sunday in 2028 falls on 16 April. Expect Holy Week (Semana Santa) from 9–16 April to be busy in Marbella and Puerto Banús. Book your Marbella boat rental at least 4–6 weeks in advance to secure your preferred vessel. Popular boats like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, includes jet ski) and the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) sell out quickly. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is a great value at €749 for 2 hours.

Best Boats for April Conditions

April’s moderate seas suit a wide range of vessels. Here are our top picks:

  • Astondoa 40 – 12.5m, 9 pax, €749/2h. Perfect for a short sunset cruise along the Golden Mile.
  • Azimut 39 – 12.5m, 11 pax, same pricing. Comfortable for a half-day trip to Cabopino.
  • Mangusta 80 – 24m, 12 pax, €4,719/4h (jet ski included). Ideal for a full-day adventure to Estepona or Sotogrande.
  • Fairline Targa 12m – 12m, 10 pax. Great for a sporty ride with a flybridge for sunbathing.
  • Bandido – 11.5m, 8 pax. A classic open boat for smaller groups wanting a lively day out.

What’s Included in Every Charter

All our rentals include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. Your skipper will also act as a guide, pointing out landmarks like La Concha mountain, Río Verde, and Cala Cortés.

April Sea Conditions & Safety

The Mediterranean in April is generally calm, but occasional Levante easterly winds can bring choppier seas. Our skippers monitor forecasts daily. If conditions are unsafe, we’ll reschedule or refund in full. For a smooth ride, morning departures (10:00–12:00) are best. Afternoon winds often pick up, but remain manageable for most boats.

Where to Go: Easter Cruise Routes

Popular April itineraries include:

  • Puerto Banús to Cabopino (~8 NM) – anchor at Cala del Faro for a sheltered swim stop.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona (~12 NM) – explore the old town and marina.
  • Puerto Banús to Sotogrande (~25 NM) – a longer cruise for a full-day charter, passing Marbella’s coastline.
  • Golden Mile sunset cruise – 2-hour evening trip with views of the Sierra Blanca.

Packing List for Your April Boat Trip

  • Light jacket or sweatshirt (morning/evening)
  • Swimsuit and towel
  • Wetsuit or swim shirt (if you plan to swim)
  • Sunscreen (SPF 30+), sunglasses, hat
  • Windbreaker
  • Camera or phone for photos
  • Comfortable non-slip shoes
